reel_script.onscreen: Reputation is verified at procurement gates.
reel_script.voiceover: In industrial B2B, corporate reputation is decided by audit teams checking regulatory compliance and supply chain data.
reel_script.direction: Text transition emphasizing procurement verification over marketing copy.

reel_script.voiceover: Gate one: Primary emissions data. If your sustainability report relies on industry averages rather than site-level metering, procurement rejects it.
reel_script.direction: Onscreen checklist graphic highlighting primary data requirement.

reel_script.voiceover: Gate two: Sub-tier safety logs. Corporate comms publishes policy guidelines, but auditors verify lost-time injury rates across sub-contractors.
reel_script.direction: Onscreen graphic displaying safety audit checks.

reel_script.voiceover: Gate three: Chain of custody waste logs. Broad pledge statements fail without manifest records from secondary processors.
reel_script.direction: Visual showing waste tracking manifest requirement.

reel_script.voiceover: Build ESG communication that is not greenwashing by grounding claims in documentation your procurement team already submits to regulators.
reel_script.direction: Final summary card displaying the core operational principle.

caption:
Your PR release won't survive a vendor audit.

Executing ESG communication that is not greenwashing requires aligning corporate communications with operational proof.

In B2B and heavy industry, enterprise buyers do not read slick CSR brochures. Procurement committees run vendor audits using strict compliance checklists.

If your comms team publishes targets that operations cannot back up with site-level logs, you create commercial risk. The auditor spots the gap, the vendor score drops, and contract renewal stalls.

Stop writing broad pledge statements. Use the exact datasets your regulatory teams submit during compliance reviews.

Reputation is an operational record, not a promotional campaign.

Send this to whoever is reviewing your corporate comms strategy before the next audit cycle.
